title: Pico de gallo
subtitle: Mexican fresh tomato salsa
excerpt: Finely diced fresh tomato, white onion, jalapeño, coriander, and lime juice. No cooking. The Mexican kitchen staple that goes with tacos, grilled meat, scrambled eggs, and everything in between.
sourceNotes: Pico de gallo (also called salsa fresca or salsa cruda) is a fundamental preparation of Mexican cooking. Cross-referenced with Diana Kennedy, The Cuisines of Mexico (1972).

recipe.batchNotes: Best made fresh; flavour holds for up to 4 hours. Keeps in the fridge overnight but the tomato softens.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Rest for 15 minutes before serving to allow the flavours to meld.

content.text: Pico de gallo is a knife salsa: everything diced finely and roughly evenly, tossed with lime juice and salt. There is no blending, no cooking, no pureeing. The quality of the tomatoes matters greatly. Use ripe, flavourful tomatoes; pale supermarket tomatoes produce a flat result. In winter, use good-quality cherry tomatoes instead.

items.prepNote: ripe, about 500 g, seeds removed, finely diced
seeds removed for less heat, finely diced
finely chopped, leaves and tender stems

content.text: Halve the tomatoes and scoop out the seeds and watery pulp with a spoon. Finely dice the flesh into about 5 mm pieces.
Combine the diced tomato, white onion, jalapeño, and coriander in a bowl. Add the lime juice and salt. Toss well.
Leave to rest for 15 minutes before serving. Taste and adjust: more lime for sharpness, more salt, more jalapeño for heat.

items.cause: Seeds and pulp not removed or tomatoes over-rested
items.fix: Always deseed the tomatoes first. Serve within 2 to 3 hours of making.

items.cause: Raw white onion can be aggressive
items.fix: Rinse the diced onion under cold water and pat dry before adding. This removes the sharpest compounds.

items.cause: Under-salted or tomatoes not ripe enough
items.fix: Add more salt and a squeeze of lime. Use cherry tomatoes in place of bland vine tomatoes.

items.cause: Jalapeño seeds included or very hot variety
items.fix: Remove all jalapeño seeds and white membrane. Use half a jalapeño next time.

content.text: Pico de gallo is one of the fundamental condiments of Mexican cooking. The name means 'beak of the rooster', possibly a reference to the way it was once eaten pinched between thumb and forefinger. It is distinct from cooked salsas and from the blended salsas verdes and rojas: where those rely on roasted or cooked ingredients, pico de gallo is entirely fresh. It goes with almost everything: tacos, grilled fish, scrambled eggs, chips, or simply eaten with spoons from the bowl.
